catalog_quote: 1.2. The Intonation. Intonation is very important in order to speak Pokot language well. The intonation is often the only difference between two given words, while the phonems are the same. The intonation helps to distinguish: The singular form of a noun from its plural. The accusative case of a noun from the nominative case. The subject from the object in a sentence. The meaning of a word. This is very common in the verbs. ... Types of tones. In Pokot language there are four types of tones: a High tone. Transcribed in this book as "´". b Low tone. For which we do not write any symbol. c High-low tone. ... d Low-high tone. ... The combined tones ( c,d.) make the vowel a bit longer. They appear above all in the dyptongues. ... According to our research in musical terms the difference between the "low" and the "high" tones is of "two tones" (usually Do and Mi on the Natural scale). ... […

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding passages are verbatim in held files at the stated places (Herreros Baroja 1989 pp. 11-12 page images; Beech 1911 pp. 49-50 djvu text). (2) The classification 'tonal (four tones, lexical + grammatical; no stress rule stated)' rests on a 1989 missionary/learner grammar, which is not a linguist's phonology, but it is one of only two full grammars of Pokot, the only open one, and its content (H, L, HL, LH; tone marks number, case, verb class) agrees with everything known about Kalenjin prosody (Tucker & Bryan, Creider, Rottland, Dimmendaal all analyse Kalenjin lects as tone languages with tonal case). Glottolog (24 refs, fetched sources now) and the Glottolog 5.1 master bib list no phonology, tone study, dissertation or JIPA illustration for Pökoot; repository and API searches that still worked (UoN DSpace, Crossref, archive.
